scenes.name: Takeoff

lines.text: Five TBM Avenger torpedo bombers lift off on a routine training flight. Fourteen men aboard.

caption: DECEMBER 5, 1945 · 2:10 PM
NAVAL AIR STATION FORT LAUDERDALE, FLORIDA

lines.text: Ninety minutes later, the flight leader, Lieutenant Charles Taylor, believes both of his compasses have failed... and that he is over the Florida Keys.

scenes.name: Radio

lines.text: Both of my compasses are out, and I am trying to find Fort Lauderdale, Florida. I'm sure I'm in the Keys, but I don't know how far down.
lines.label: LT. CHARLES TAYLOR · FT-28

lines.text: Put the sun on your port wing if you are in the Keys, and fly up the coast until you get to Miami.
lines.label: LT. ROBERT COX · FT-74

caption: RADIO EXCHANGE RECONSTRUCTED FROM THE U.S. NAVY INVESTIGATION
NO AUDIO RECORDINGS EXIST

lines.text: Flight one-nine, Fort Lauderdale. Switch to three thousand kilocycles. Say your position.
lines.label: FORT LAUDERDALE RADIO

lines.text: Radio direction finders placed them north of the Bahamas, far out over the open Atlantic. The fix came too late.

scenes.name: The sixth aircraft

lines.text: All planes close up tight. We'll have to ditch unless landfall. When the first plane drops below ten gallons, we all go down together.
lines.label: LT. CHARLES TAYLOR · FT-28

caption: FICTIONAL ELEMENT
beat: THEN, BESIDE THEM IN THE FOG... A SIXTH.

scenes.name: The rescue

lines.text: A PBM Mariner flying boat, thirteen men aboard, took off to search for them.
Twenty-three minutes later, the crew of a tanker saw flames on the sea. The USS Solomons watched a radar contact... disappear.

caption: NAVAL AIR STATION BANANA RIVER · 7:27 PM

scenes.name: The dead frequency

lines.text: Fort Lauderdale... Flight nineteen... we're still flying.
lines.label: UNKNOWN STATION

caption: DECADES LATER
FICTIONAL HORROR DRAMATIZATION
end: Radio lines in this film are reconstructed from the U.S. Navy investigation; no recordings exist.
The sixth aircraft and the final transmission are fiction.
